findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so the strategy provides no backpressure
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates every work queue with queue.Queue() and no maxsize, and submit() therefore never blocks or raises MessageRejected. The Arroyo processor can keep polling Kafka and enqueueing messages faster than workers process them, causing unbounded memory growth in both the queues and OffsetTracker's offset sets and potentially an OOM. This also contradicts the strategy docstring's claim of natural backpressure when queues fill up.

findings.title: Failed work items are marked complete and their offsets are committed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run catches any exception from result_processor, logs it, and then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in the finally block. The commit loop can consequently commit offsets for messages whose processing failed, so those Kafka messages will not be redelivered or sent to a DLQ. This contradicts the strategy's stated guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing.

findings.title: Shutdown flag causes workers to abandon queued items
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before shutting down the queues, while OrderedQueueWorker.run checks that flag at the top of every loop iteration. A worker blocked in get() may process at most one queued item after shutdown begins and then exit, leaving the rest of its queue unprocessed despite queue.shutdown(immediate=False) being intended to drain it. Graceful shutdown therefore strands accepted work; those offsets remain uncompleted and the messages must be reprocessed after restart.

findings.title: Commit loop is stopped before queued work is drained
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close sets shutdown_event and joins the commit thread before calling queue_pool.shutdown(). Any offsets completed by workers while the pool is draining afterwards have no commit thread left to commit them, so successfully processed messages are not checkpointed on graceful close and will be delivered and processed again after restart.

findings.title: Closing a strategy destroys the shared pool reused after rebalance
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool and passes that same object to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy it creates, but this strategy's close() shuts the shared pool down. Arroyo closes and joins the old strategy when partitions are revoked and then creates a new strategy from the same factory for the new assignment, so the new strategy reuses queues that are already shut down and workers that have exited. Subsequent puts raise queue.ShutDown, which SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches and then marks the offset complete, allowing unprocessed messages to be committed and permanently lost after a routine rebalance.
